\textbf{Source.} Tadelis (2013), \emph{Game Theory: An Introduction}, Exercise 5.2 ``Weak Dominance'', p.~95 {[}PDF p.~114{]}. Answer in the source: none (the preface, p.~xiii, says about half of the exercises are solved on Princeton UP's website). Reproduced verbatim.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{Weak Dominance:} A strategy \(s^W \in S\) is a weakly dominant strategy equilibrium if \(s_i^W \in S_i\) is a weakly dominant strategy for all \(i \in N\), that is, if \(v_i(s_i^W, s_{-i}) \ge v_i(s_i', s_{-i})\) for all \(s_i' \in S_i\) and for all \(s_{-i} \in S_{-i}\). Provide an example of a game for which there is a weakly dominant strategy equilibrium as well as another Nash equilibrium.
\end{quote}
